newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan campaign rules keep dead candidate on TV.
newsitem.headline: Japan campaign rules keep dead candidate on TV.

text.p: The dead may no longer vote under Japan's ever-stricter election laws, but rigid restrictions have kept the advertisement of a deceased candidate on television to the chagrin of his supporters.

Footage of Saburo Toida, a former health minister who collapsed and died while campaigning last week, is included in his Liberal Democratic Party's TV ads aired daily before Sunday's general elections, Kyodo news agency reported.

Calls for the removal of the footage -- out of fear that voters will spoil their ballots by writing in the late Toida's name instead of his son and successor -- have been rebuffed by the Home Affairs Ministry.
It is forbidden to edit, delete or re-record a campaign videotape after it has been submitted by a party for broadcasting, the ministry said.
Present law allows for the suspension of a televised advertisement only in the event that all of a party's candidates in a prefecture die, Kyodo quoted officials as saying.
